definitions.explanation: A cuckoo that arrives in Japan in early summer and calls loudly, even at night. In classical poetry it is the bird of early summer, as the bush warbler is of spring.

examples.japanese: ホトトギス⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
ホトトギス⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れ→訪れ：14267_otozure⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げる→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧⟦{鳥|とり}→鳥：00679_tori⟧だ。
examples.english: The lesser cuckoo is a bird that announces the arrival of summer.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{鳴|な}かぬ→鳴く：04388_naku⟧なら⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{待|ま}とう→待つ：00469_matsu⟧ホトトギス」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}→徳川家康：31006_tokugawaieyasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{表|あらわ}した→表す：01868_arawasu⟧⟦{句|く}→句：02137_ku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: "If the cuckoo won't sing, wait until it does" is said to describe the character of Tokugawa Ieyasu.

notes:
Kanji spellings include {時鳥|ほととぎす}, {杜鵑|ほととぎす} and {不如帰|ほととぎす}; the last is the title of a famous Meiji novel. Its call is rendered テッペンカケタカ or, playfully, ⟦{特許|とっきょ}→特許：13467_tokkyo⟧{許可局|きょかきょく}.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Three well-known verses contrast the great unifiers of Japan by what each would do with a cuckoo that will not sing:
- ⟦{織田信長|おだのぶなが}→織田信長：30992_odanobunaga⟧: ⟦{鳴|な}かぬ→鳴く：04388_naku⟧なら⟦{殺|ころ}して→殺す：01944_korosu⟧しまえホトトギス (kill it)
- ⟦{豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし}→豊臣秀吉：30993_toyotomihideyoshi⟧: ⟦{鳴|な}かぬ→鳴く：04388_naku⟧なら⟦{鳴|な}かせて→鳴く：04388_naku⟧みようホトトギス (make it sing)
- ⟦{徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}→徳川家康：31006_tokugawaieyasu⟧: ⟦{鳴|な}かぬ→鳴く：04388_naku⟧なら⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{待|ま}とう→待つ：00469_matsu⟧ホトトギス (wait until it sings)
